Definition: booths of (the) daughters; brothels, i.e. idoalatrous tents for impure purpose
BiblicalUsage: The booths of the daughters are the idolatrous tents the Babylonians set up in Samaria, shrines for impure worship. The name appears once, in the list of the gods the settlers brought with them. The booths are the opposite of the feast of booths: a holy shelter turned into a brothel.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the booths of the daughters show how a holy thing can be twisted into an unholy one, and the land is judged for it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
